sentences.text: The Australian Public Service Commission and Merit Protection Commissioner reported on their work in 2025–26, covering public service capability, integrity, workforce management and employment reviews.
sentences.support:
This report reflects our work to strengthen APS capability, 
maintain public trust, support a high-performing workforce

sentences.text: The Commission assessed six measures of its performance and reported achieving four, substantially achieving one and partly achieving one.
sentences.support:
we achieved the targets for 4 measures, substantially achieved the 
targets for one measure, and partially achieved the targets for one measure.

sentences.text: The Merit Protection Commissioner reported receiving 109 applications to review Code of Conduct decisions and 199 applications concerning other employment decisions.
sentences.support:
We received 199 applications from  
APS employees seeking a review of  
an employment decisions (other than  
Code of Conduct decisions).

sentences.text: The Merit Protection Commissioner reported recommending that 40% of reviewed Code of Conduct breach or sanction decisions be set aside or varied.
sentences.section: Our year at a glance; Review outcomes
sentences.support:
We set aside/varied 40% of decisions of 
Code of Conduct breaches and sanctions 
that we reviewed.

sentences.text: The Merit Protection Commissioner concluded that recurring problems in these decisions showed a continuing gap in agencies' ability to manage misconduct and apply the Code of Conduct.
sentences.support:
continues to highlight a 
significant capability gap in the management of misconduct and the application of the Code 
of Conduct.

sentences.text: The Merit Protection Commissioner reported that all recommendations it made to agency heads in 2025–26 were accepted and implemented.
sentences.support:
All the recommendations made by the MPC to agency 
heads in 2025–26 were accepted and implemented.

findings.quote:
However, we did observe that, once a declaration is made, the consideration of specific 
and relevant strategies on how to best manage the conflict is often cursory and 
seemingly perfunctory.
Overall, the Commission achieved its purpose for the reporting period.

All the recommendations made by the MPC to agency 
heads in 2025–26 were accepted and implemented.

notes: This is a combined annual report, rather than an inquiry with a report-wide recommendations list; no overall recommendation count is inferred. The Commission’s review on PDF pages 8-9 is recorded as its own summary equivalent. The separate Merit Protection Commissioner’s foreword on PDF pages 140-141 and year-at-a-glance overview on PDF page 144 were also read, along with review findings and recommendations. Financial statement PDF pages 57-94 contain only headers or whitespace in the supplied text; PDF page 56 contains only the financial statements heading and header. No financial results are summarised. No named individuals are included.
